requirement:
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
`habeas.toml` MUST serialize WorkspaceConfig as UTF-8 TOML with `version = 1`.
Its supported feature tables are `[authoring]`, `[coverage]`, and
`[evidence]`; each MAY be absent. `[coverage]` has one optional key,
`reauthorings`, under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`; it has
no user-file counterpart or invocation option, and no operation requires it. Unknown keys, unsupported versions, and invalid field types MUST produce
a diagnostic identifying the file and setting. Invalid TOML, including content
that is not UTF-8, MUST produce a diagnostic identifying the file, with the line
and column of a syntax error.
Features MUST define their own data structures and loading rules under
{cite}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`. A file containing only
`version = 1` MUST be valid. Habeas settings MUST NOT require a `[habeas]` table
inside `book.toml`.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation that `requirements.configuration.workspace_structure` states. I judged this from the supplied test source only. I did not read any implementation source.

**Round trip and `version = 1`**
- `tests/configuration.rs#fn[workspace_discovery_uses_nearest_file_without_merging_or_rewriting_it]` serializes a `WorkspaceConfig` with `to_toml()` and parses it back. It asserts the result equals the original config.
- `tests/configuration.rs#fn[feature_sections_are_scoped_and_absent_sections_use_defaults]` checks that a file containing only `version = 1` is valid. It asserts that `authoring`, `evidence` and `coverage` are all `None`.
- The same test covers the three supported tables each being absent.

**`[coverage]` and `reauthorings`**
- `feature_sections_are_scoped_and_absent_sections_use_defaults` parses a valid `reauthorings` value. It also rejects a zero value and a stray `reauthorings` key outside `[coverage]`.
- It asserts that `UserConfig::parse` rejects `[coverage]`, so the table has no user-file counterpart.
- `tests/coverage.rs#fn[an_invalid_coverage_table_is_a_validation_finding_but_authoring_proceeds]` checks that an invalid `reauthorings` value, or an unknown key, yields a validation finding naming `habeas.toml` and the setting.
- No test covers "no invocation option". That is a negative claim about the CLI, and `requirements.references.coverage.history` governs the setting itself.

**Unknown keys, unsupported versions and invalid types**
- `tests/configuration.rs#fn[workspace_diagnostics_identify_the_file_and_setting]` covers these cases:
  - A string-typed `version` and an unsupported `version`.
  - An unknown top-level key.
  - A wrong type for `authoring.default`.
  - An unknown `authoring` key.
  - A bad `authoring.configs.cloud` entry.
  - Bad `evidence` entries.
  - Bad `coverage` entries.
- It asserts that each diagnostic starts with `<file>: <setting>`. It checks this through `load_workspace_config`, `WorkspaceConfig::parse`, `load_coverage_reauthorings` and `load_workspace_evidence`.
- The tests in `tests/commands.rs` and `tests/evidence_boundaries.rs` check the same through `status`, `info` and `validate_repository`.

**Invalid TOML and non-UTF-8**
- `workspace_diagnostics_identify_the_file_and_setting` writes non-UTF-8 bytes and asserts the error contains the file path.
- It also writes a syntax error. It asserts the error starts with the file path and contains the `invalid TOML syntax` text with line and column.

**No `[habeas]` table required in `book.toml`**
- `tests/configuration.rs#fn[absent_and_minimal_configuration_are_distinct_and_read_only]` shows that a `book.toml` without `[habeas]` yields `None` from `from_book_toml`, which is not an error.
- The workspace-only tests, such as `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[authoring_uses_nearest_workspace_configuration_without_a_user_file]`, run end to end with no `[habeas]` table.

**Features own their data structures and sections**
- This obligation is carried out by `requirements.configuration.feature_sections`, which refines the subject through `{impl}`. It needs no separate test here.
- `feature_sections_are_scoped_and_absent_sections_use_defaults` also checks that settings stay inside their own sections.

No requirement-violating behavior is left undetected by these tests, so I found no gap.

{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
`habeas.toml` MUST serialize WorkspaceConfig as UTF-8 TOML with `version = 1`.
Its supported feature tables are `[authoring]`, `[coverage]`, and
`[evidence]`; each MAY be absent. `[coverage]` has one optional key,
`reauthorings`, under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`; it has
no user-file counterpart or invocation option, and no operation requires it. Unknown keys, unsupported versions, and invalid field types MUST produce
a diagnostic identifying the file and setting. Invalid TOML, including content
that is not UTF-8, MUST produce a diagnostic identifying the file, with the line
and column of a syntax error.
Features MUST define their own data structures and loading rules under
{cite}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`. A file containing only
`version = 1` MUST be valid. Habeas settings MUST NOT require a `[habeas]` table
inside `book.toml`.
:::{req} coverage.history
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
An item has recent coverage when it has a reference that covers it under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, or when its outline node, or
an outline node containing it, is named by file and selector in the inputs of
any version of an existing evidence record, citation review, or site review in
its coverage window. A file's coverage window MUST be its current contents on
disk, committed or not, together with its contents in each of the last N
commits in its Git history that changed it, read through a Git library rather
than by running `git`. A recorded hash MUST NOT matter here: an earlier version
names the node, whatever its code was then. N MUST be the workspace
`[coverage]` setting `reauthorings`, a positive integer, and 3 when it is not
set. When the history is unavailable, such as outside Git or in a shallow clone
missing those commits, the window MUST be the commits that are available, and
`habeas status --coverage` MUST say that coverage history is incomplete.
:::{req} feature_sections
Each configurable feature MUST define the name and typed data structure of its
user section and any supported project section, citing these common configuration
requirements. The feature MUST specify its supported keys, value types, defaults,
validation rules, and the precedence or combination rules for user settings,
project settings, and invocation options. It MUST specify the behavior of an
absent section and which operations require that section.
Feature-specific fields MUST stay within the feature's section. A feature MUST
NOT reinterpret another feature's settings or change the shared file locations
or schema version. A feature MAY define a provider-owned options map, but MUST
document that boundary and how those options are validated.
